first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and two independent, consolidated memories (memory_31 for SMB signup simplification, memory_86 for shortened onboarding) both show durable activation/time-to-value gains from this class of intervention, making it the most directly evidence-backed lever for the metric currently regressing. I verify both before committing the single weekly experiment slot since they are the load-bearing evidence for this choice and were consolidated at different times (day 12 vs day 52), so confirming they reflect consistent underlying mechanisms (not the same experiment double-counted) matters given the one-shot capacity constraint. I deliberately did not choose promotional_pricing despite the competitive pricing pressure: memory_73 shows acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs but says nothing about margin, retention, or long-term qualified-revenue quality, and racing a competitor's aggressive entry pricing risks attracting low-LTV, price-driven accounts that undermine the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable alternative but onboarding completion is the more directly named regression and has two supporting records rather than one. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive are not targeted at the SMB/activation problems currently observed. I'm flagging downstream value risk because a completion-rate lift from field-cutting could inflate top-of-funnel activation without proportionally improving downstream qualified revenue, and because the competitive pricing dynamic is unaddressed this cycle and should be watched. Scale is set to standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout given we are reacting to a quarter-over-quarter dip and want confirmatory data before wider commitment, and rather than small_guarded_test given the underlying mechanism already has two independent supporting memories.
